title: Lena year matching accounted for 97% of a three-river peak excess in 31 certified years from 1980 to 2011
abstract: We kept Ob-Yenisey river-year pairs intact and shuffled only Lena years within fixed periods. In 31 complete certified years from 1980 to 2011, matching Lena years gave a 1.68% excess in the mean April-August seven-day peak of summed gauge flow. The two-sided conditional permutation p value was 0.0448. An exact accounting check assigned 96.99% of the excess over fully independent river-year pairing to this conditional term. This fraction depends on the order of the shuffles and is not a causal fraction. Equal seasonal volumes gave 1.57% and p = 0.0585. In 29 separate earlier certified years from 1936 to 1975, the raw estimate was 0.95%, with p = 0.1956. Thus the earlier data did not give clear support. Five-year and circular checks changed statistical support. The recent result extends prior tests by preserving the Ob-Yenisey relation. It uses the same source and gauges. Short records, source error, regulation and exchangeability limit inference. No coastal pulse, cause or change between periods is established. The package contains code, exact source hashes, aggregate results, null draws, a figure and reproduction instructions. External daily flow data stay outside the signed package.

display.caption: Observed conditional peak excess and aggregate permutation null distributions. Null distributions are not confidence intervals.
